cards.text: Last time, the men of Gibeah abused a Levite's concubine until she died, and he sent her body in pieces throughout Israel (Judges 19:25-29). Now all the Israelites, from Dan to Beersheba and from the land of Gilead, gather as one man before the LORD at Mizpah. That's 400,000 men on foot, armed with swords.
Meanwhile, the Benjamites hear that Israel has gone up to Mizpah. Back at the assembly, the Israelites have a question.

cards.question: What do the Israelites gathered at Mizpah want to know?

answers.text: Who will be king over them

cards.text: The Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answers. He says he and his concubine came to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.

cards.question: The Levite tells the assembly that the men of Gibeah surrounded the house that night and intended to kill him.

cards.text: Then he says they abused his concubine, and she died. Notice what he leaves out: back in Judges 19:25, he's the one who sent her outside to them.

cards.question: The Levite says he cut his concubine into pieces and sent her throughout Israel. What reason does he give the assembly?

answers.text: Gibeah's men did a disgraceful act in Israel
He wanted the tribes to choose a king
He wanted Benjamin to pay him back

cards.text: Then he hands it to the crowd: "Behold, all you Israelites, give your advice and verdict here and now." And all the people stand up as one man.

cards.question: Standing as one man, what do the people say about going home?

answers.text: Not one of them will go home
Each of them will go home to pray
Only the leaders will stay behind

cards.text: Then they make a plan for Gibeah: they'll go against it as the lot dictates. But an army this big needs more than swords.

cards.question: They'll take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes to supply ___ for the army.

cards.text: So all the men of Israel gather as one man, united against the city. Then they send men throughout the tribe of Benjamin to ask, "What is this wickedness that has occurred among you?"

cards.question: Israel's message to Benjamin: hand over the wicked men of ___ so they can be put to death and Israel can be purged of this evil.
The Benjamites listen to their fellow Israelites and hand the men of Gibeah over.

cards.text: One question, one right answer, and Benjamin picks the other one. The Benjamites come together at Gibeah to fight Israel: 26,000 swordsmen from their cities, plus 700 select men of Gibeah.

cards.question: Among all of Benjamin's soldiers are 700 select left-handers. What can each of them do?

answers.text: Sling a stone at a hair without missing
Shoot an arrow through a ring
Throw a spear across a river

cards.question: Not counting Benjamin, the rest of Israel's army is smaller than Benjamin's.

cards.text: Israel, apart from Benjamin, has 400,000 swordsmen, each one an experienced warrior. But Benjamin's slingers hit a HAIR, friend, and I miss the cookie sheet from six inches away with a mustache for HANDS.
Israel sets out, goes up to Bethel and asks God, "Who of us shall go up first to fight against the Benjamites?"

cards.question: The LORD answers Israel's question: ___ will be first.

cards.text: The next morning they camp near Gibeah and take up their battle positions. It's 400,000 against about 27,000, so on paper this one's over before the timer goes off.

cards.question: Israel's huge army wins easily on the first day at Gibeah.

cards.text: The Benjamites come out of Gibeah and cut down 22,000 Israelites that day. Friend, I've read this one a lot of times, and that line still stops me.
But Israel takes courage and lines up again in the same place they stood on the first day.

cards.question: Before they fight again, the Israelites go up before the LORD until evening. What are they doing there?

answers.text: Weeping and asking Him what to do
Building an altar out of stones
Reading the Law out loud together

cards.question: When Israel asks about fighting their brothers the Benjamites again, the LORD tells them to go up against them.

cards.text: So on the second day, Israel advances. And once again, the Benjamites come out of Gibeah against them.

cards.question: How does the second day of fighting go for Israel?

answers.text: Benjamin runs back inside the walls
Both armies pull back before noon

cards.text: Two days, 40,000 men down. So all the people go up to Bethel and sit weeping before the LORD.

cards.question: Besides weeping before the LORD at Bethel, what else do the Israelites do that day?

cards.text: They inquire of the LORD again. The ark of the covenant of God is there, and Phinehas son of Eleazar, Aaron's grandson, serves before it.

cards.question: This time, Israel also asks the LORD whether they should stop fighting the Benjamites.
The LORD tells Israel to fight. What does He promise them this time?

answers.text: He'll deliver Benjamin into their hand tomorrow
Judah will win the battle alone tomorrow
Benjamin will give up within seven days

cards.text: Friend, after two days like that, hearing God say "tomorrow" changes EVERYTHING. So Israel sets up an ambush around Gibeah, and on the third day they line up against the city just like before.

cards.question: On the third day, the Benjamites attack Israel just as before. Where does the fighting take them?

cards.text: They kill about thirty men of Israel out on the roads. "We are defeating them as before," say the Benjamites.

cards.question: Israel's plan is to retreat and draw the Benjamites away from the city onto the roads.

cards.text: Friend, never celebrate while the other army is walking backward ON PURPOSE. All Israel lines up at Baal-tamar, and the men in ambush charge out from west of Gibeah.
Then 10,000 select men from all Israel make a frontal assault on Gibeah, and the battle is fierce.

cards.question: During the fierce battle at Gibeah, the Benjamites can tell that disaster is coming for them.
Israel has the ambush and the numbers. But who does the text say defeats Benjamin that day?

cards.text: That day, Israel strikes down 25,100 Benjamites, all armed with swords. Then the Benjamites realize they've been defeated.

cards.question: Earlier in the battle, Israel kept retreating before Benjamin. Why were they doing it?

answers.text: They were relying on the ambush
They were running out of men

cards.text: The men in ambush rush suddenly against Gibeah and put the whole city to the sword.

cards.question: Israel's signal with the men in ambush: when a great cloud of ___ goes up from the city, the men of Israel will ___ in the battle.

cards.text: The Benjamites look behind them and see the whole city going up in smoke. Friend, I know smoke, and when it comes out of MY oven, something has gone VERY wrong.

cards.question: When the men of Israel turn back on them, the men of Benjamin are terrified.
The Benjamites flee toward the wilderness and get away without the battle catching them.

cards.text: Israel surrounds them near Gibeah on the east, and 18,000 fall there, then 5,000 more on the roads and 2,000 at Gidom. That day, 25,000 Benjamite swordsmen fall, all men of valor.

cards.question: But 600 Benjamite men turn and flee into the wilderness. Where do they go?

cards.text: They stay there four months. I spent years in a junk drawer, so I know a little about sitting somewhere, waiting to see what happens next.

cards.question: Meanwhile, the men of Israel turn back against the other Benjamites. What happens to the cities in their path?

cards.text: They put all those cities to the sword, including the animals and everything else they find. We'll pause right there, friend, but don't shut the oven on this one, because there's more coming.
